en: The Philippine eagle, our national bird, lives exclusively in the tall, undisturbed tropical rainforests of Mindanao.
Our national flower, the sampaguita, releases its sweet fragrance mostly at night to attract moth pollinators.
National Scientist Ramon Barba discovered that spraying mango trees with potassium nitrate solution makes them bloom abundantly.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into steep mountains, creating stone steps that prevent soil erosion.
The carabao, our national animal, cools its body by wallowing in muddy water during hot afternoons.
Jose Rizal planted fruit trees and built a water system in Dapitan, leaving observable environmental improvements.
The narra, our national tree, drops its small yellow flowers in spring, covering the forest floor brightly.
During the Lucban Pahiyas Festival, locals decorate their houses with colorful kiping made from ground rice.
Marine biologist Angel Alcala established protected coral reef sanctuaries to help observable fish populations recover from overfishing.
The South Sea pearl, our national gem, forms inside the mantle of large oysters found in Palawan.
The Tboli people weave tnalak cloth by extracting strong, natural fibers from the stalks of abaca plants.
The bangus, our national fish, thrives in coastal fishpens where it grazes on visible algae and plankton.
